A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bayesian Sample Inference by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; v2 also includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original BSI likelihood results on CIFAR10, ImageNet32, and ImageNet64, sampling-quality experiments, and empirical analyses of ELBO convergence and variance reduction.

after.justification: V2 reports original likelihood and FID comparisons on ImageNet32, retained CIFAR10 results, convergence and variance analyses, and generated samples.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, posterior updates, prior, importance sampling, preconditioning, and backbone designs are retained. Section 3.4 changes the stated loss normalization from L∞_M/n to 2L∞_M/n, consistent with the already unchanged Algorithm 2; this supports a documentation correction rather than a changed procedure.

E1.justification: CIFAR10 and ImageNet32 remain, but ImageNet64 training, evaluation, and generated samples are removed. This narrows coverage by dropping 64×64 image generation while retaining the same image domains.

E2.justification: V1 Table 2 compares against Flow Matching, i-DODE, VDM, and BFN. V2 removes Flow Matching and i-DODE from the reported comparisons and focuses on VDM and BFN, adding ImageNet32 BFN results where v1 reported none. The CIFAR10 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: For ImageNet32, Appendix E changes the reported training budget from 10M to 2M steps and learning rate from 2×10^-4 to 5×10^-4, with v2 specifying cosine decay to 5×10^-5. The new comparison trains all three methods with DiT-L-2 and specifies five measurement-term and two reconstruction-term ELBO samples, plus FID from 50,000 unconditional samples generated in 1024 steps.

E4.justification: V1's linear-versus-EDM7 schedule sensitivity analysis on CIFAR10 and ImageNet32 is removed. V2 instead compares BSI, BFN, and VDM across sampling-step counts on ImageNet32. V1's preliminary DiT overfitting and architecture-comparison findings disappear, while ELBO convergence and importance-sampling variance analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 Table 2 introduces means and standard deviations over three training seeds for ImageNet32, whereas v1 reports point estimates. V2 also explicitly discloses single-run CIFAR10 training. The Figure 4 noise-floor definition changes from the sum of two estimator standard deviations to the standard deviation of their difference.

E6.justification: V2 Table 2 reports ImageNet32 BPD/FID of 3.448±0.006/8.9±0.1 for BSI, 3.452±0.006/9.9±0.5 for VDM, and 3.448±0.005/11.0±0.1 for BFN. These replace v1's broader likelihood table under revised settings, so they do not establish a same-setting performance change. ImageNet64 results and schedule-comparison results disappear; CIFAR10 Table 3 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The posterior-update result, finite- and infinite-step ELBOs, prior results, BFN special-case argument, diffusion connection, and preconditioning derivation are retained, including their appendix proofs. Equation renumbering and equivalent fraction formatting do not introduce substantive theoretical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace claims of likelihood superiority over VDM and BFN with equivalent likelihoods and better ImageNet32 sample quality. The broader competitive-density-estimation claim is narrowed. The methodological and theoretical contribution claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the unchanged CIFAR10 likelihood differences as equivalence rather than improvement and connects the new FID ordering to increasing initial-state variance. It removes v1's direct attribution of likelihood gains to encoder simplicity, discussion of DiT overfitting, and explanation of EDM7's advantage. The general encoder-learning hypothesis in Appendix A remains.

D1.justification: V2 documents cosine warm-up from 10^-8, adds dataset-license/access information and a checklist code-release statement, and revises the training tables. V1's explicit sampling-schedule recipe and ImageNet64 configuration details are removed. Hardware, throughput, EMA, low-discrepancy sampling, and the implementation link remain documented.

R1.justification: The Zheng et al. (2024) i-DODE reference is removed, and empirical positioning shifts from a broader likelihood comparison toward closely related BFN and VDM. Most citations and the substantive related-model discussion in Section 4 and Appendix A are retained.

P1.justification: V2 clarifies introductory and sampling notation and reorganizes Section 6 from likelihood/sample-quality subsections into ImageNet32/CIFAR10 subsections. Generated samples move from Appendix E.2 to F, and licensing and checklist sections are added. Most method and proof prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with substantial reflow of algorithms, equations, and tables. Table 2 is rebuilt around BPD/FID with uncertainty; the schedule plots and multiple sample galleries are replaced by a method-comparison plot and three-method ImageNet32 gallery. Existing conceptual and convergence figures are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: V1's ImageNet comparison explicitly relied partly on scores from unavailable older dataset versions. V2 replaces this with a matched ImageNet32 comparison using the same backbone and training budget across methods, three-seed uncertainty, and clearly specified evaluation procedures. It also tempers unsupported likelihood-superiority claims. Losing ImageNet64 coverage and sampling-schedule guidance reduces breadth and detail, but the stronger comparability and better-calibrated central empirical claims substantially improve the paper's credibility.
